top_buys.pitch: Value-seeking holiday shoppers and distressed department stores keep funneling traffic to off-price.
top_buys.why: Today's coverage highlights consumers trading down to secondhand and value this holiday, while Macy's, Kohl's and others enter Black Friday with something to prove amid bankruptcies. Off-price chains buy excess inventory cheaply, so tariff-driven supply dislocation can actually widen their buying opportunities. Consumer staples and value retail are among the few sectors green on the week as money rotates out of technology.
top_buys.risks: A weak overall holiday spend or tariff-driven cost inflation could compress margins, and the stock already trades at a full valuation.
top_buys.watch: Black Friday/Cyber Monday traffic data and TJX's next quarterly report.

top_buys.pitch: Drones, mines and missile strikes across the Gulf and Europe keep the defense order book filling.
top_buys.why: Houthis hit Saudi Arabia's largest refinery and Riyadh's tallest tower and are threatening Red Sea ports, Iran says ships struck mines in Hormuz, and the UK is hangaring aircraft over drone threats. That mix drives demand for air and missile defense, counter-drone systems and ISR, which are core L3Harris products. Defense is also a defensive place to be while the AI complex de-rates.
top_buys.risks: Defense stocks have lagged this year despite contract wins, and budget timing means headlines often don't convert into revenue quickly.
top_buys.watch: New Middle East munitions and counter-drone contract awards over the next few weeks.

top_buys.company: Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund
top_buys.pitch: Hotter inflation, stronger growth and risk-off flows all point the same way for the dollar.
top_buys.why: Q3 GDP was revised sharply higher with inflation broadening out, which pushes back against near-term Fed cuts and has commentators discussing a December hike. Risk-off markets are already lifting the dollar and weighing on gold. This is a low-volatility way to express the rate story without owning a single stock.
top_buys.risks: A soft jobs or CPI print would flip rate-cut expectations and knock the dollar back quickly.
top_buys.watch: The next CPI release and Fed speakers ahead of the December meeting.

top_buys.pitch: Classic defensive beneficiary of the rotation out of AI names.
top_buys.why: Consumer staples rose about 1.4% last week while technology fell more than 5%, as investors sought shelter from the AI unwind and rate worries. P&G is a low-volatility, dividend-paying anchor that tends to attract flows in exactly this environment. Nothing in today's news hurts it directly.
top_buys.risks: A sharp tech rebound would reverse the rotation, and a stronger dollar hurts P&G's overseas earnings.
top_buys.watch: Whether staples keep outperforming if the Nasdaq stabilizes.

top_buys.pitch: Food inflation and value-focused shoppers support grocery volumes and pricing.
top_buys.why: Turkey prices are at records and retailers are leaning into cheap holiday meal bundles, which drives traffic into grocers. Grocery is a defensive earnings stream at a time when investors are shedding high-multiple tech. Staples have been one of the better performing sectors this week.
top_buys.risks: Aggressive price-war promotions from Walmart can squeeze grocer margins, and Kroger carries its own execution risk.
top_buys.watch: Kroger's next quarterly results and commentary on holiday basket size.

summary.top_pick: TJX, because value-hunting holiday shoppers and struggling department stores play straight into off-price retail, a sector that has been working while tech unwinds.
summary.watch: Whether money keeps rotating into staples, health care and the dollar, and how crude trades after the Houthi strike on Saudi Arabia's largest refinery.
